rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: I Survived This First
card.instruction: Use your experience with hardship as emotional seniority, offering guidance and judging how well others are handling the pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first restaurant review? When mine came, I made tea before opening it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've opened it. Two stars. I'm ringing the critic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the stage where I unplugged my phone. Milk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already dialled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let it ring while the tea brews. You're rushing a mistake I took all afternoon over.

card.title: I Survived This First
card.instruction: Use your experience with hardship as emotional seniority, offering guidance and judging how well others are handling the pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I went through redundancy before you. First, tidy your desk slowly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm actually excited to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Early stage. I recognise the optimism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another job. They want me there Monday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Monday? I started too soon after mine. Leave a mug here; you're not ready to make a clean break.

card.title: When We Still Believed
card.instruction: Use a shared earlier hope as your emotional home base, returning to it whenever the present feels uncertain or disappointing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This napkin still says we'll open a bookshop by the sea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We drew that before rent became real.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We also drew two chairs. We could start there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if we get rid of your desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sell it. Put 'funding our seaside bookshop' in the listing. We're making room for the first two customers.

card.title: When We Still Believed
card.instruction: Use a shared earlier hope as your emotional home base, returning to it whenever the present feels uncertain or disappointing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember when this jar was for our anniversary at the seaside?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We spent the money on the boiler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We promised we'd swim together. The boiler didn't cancel that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's in three weeks. We can afford the bus to the reservoir.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the bus fare in the jar. I'll pack the towels; we're still coming home with wet hair.

card.title: The Strong One
card.instruction: Be the strong one: steady everyone else, minimize your own needs, and resist any attempt to care for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made everyone tea. I'll call Dad's friends about the funeral.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your hands are shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's good the calls don't require trays.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sit down. I'll call. Just give me their numbers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll dial for you. Peter will cry; I'll stay on the other phone in case you need rescuing.

card.title: The Strong One
card.instruction: Be the strong one: steady everyone else, minimize your own needs, and resist any attempt to care for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the last tissue. Mum's funeral was hard on you. I've got my sleeve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're crying into both sleeves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're washable. How's your daughter holding up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asleep. Come here. You can cry on my shoulder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You'll need that shoulder when she wakes. I'll get you a dry cardigan.

card.title: Whose Pain Counts?
card.instruction: Treat every disappointment as something to measure against what you have endured, competing for whose feelings deserve greater weight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One publisher turned you down? I've kept fourteen rejection letters.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you put them away? I came here for a hug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Though fourteen rejections ought to qualify me for more than one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come here. We can both have the same hug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hold on after I let go, then. I've got thirteen more to get through.

card.title: Whose Pain Counts?
card.instruction: Treat every disappointment as something to measure against what you have endured, competing for whose feelings deserve greater weight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've been unemployed a week. I've been out a year. This coffee should really be for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought it so you'd listen to what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll listen. Mine will take longer; there's twelve months to cover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ten minutes each. I've got an interview.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An interview already? Then give me fifteen. You've started recovering.

card.title: Braver Than Me
card.instruction: Treat another person’s emotional courage as both inspiring and unfair, resenting how exposed or hesitant it makes you feel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You opened your rejection letter straight away. Must be nice, being brave on demand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was scared too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hid it very efficiently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take your time with yours. I'll leave you alone to open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, stay. I'm opening it now. You shouldn't get to be brave and considerate while I'm still finding the flap.

card.title: Braver Than Me
card.instruction: Treat another person’s emotional courage as both inspiring and unfair, resenting how exposed or hesitant it makes you feel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told them how you felt without rehearsing. I resent how impressive that was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stumbled over half of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even your stumbling looked courageous.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Want to practise with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Don't make practising look easy too.

transfer.action: I put my old coping list beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: I learned this the hard way before it had a name. {request}
transfer.response: Try my first minute before dismissing the method. {counter}
transfer.challenge: Your way might not suit me.
transfer.closing: Then at least discover what my years of practice have to offer.

transfer.action: I set {prop} beside the plan we once drew on a napkin.
transfer.opening: We believed every word on this. {request}
transfer.response: Name one part of the old hope that still fits. {counter}
transfer.closing: Together. That's the part I don't want to fold away.

transfer.action: I move {prop} within everyone's reach while hiding my shaking hand.
transfer.response: I can handle the difficult calls as well. {counter}
transfer.challenge: Who is taking care of you?
transfer.closing: We'll put that on the list after the people currently asking.

transfer.action: I place my thicker bundle of disappointments beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: I'm not comparing, but count the envelopes. {request}
transfer.response: Mine was a rough year, not just a rough week. {counter}
transfer.closing: Then it won't hurt to notice whose reference pile is larger.

transfer.action: I copy your steady breath above {prop}, with a resentful smile.
transfer.opening: You make courage look like breathing. {request}
transfer.response: I'll do it just as bravely, with a little preparation. {counter}
transfer.closing: I'd rather take the amount you needed and make it look easier.
